en: The Ritual Manual for Recitation of the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha for Eliminating Calamities and Dispelling Difficulties.
First, purify body, speech, and mind; take refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha.
Homage to the All-Illuminating Honored One and to the assembly of sages of the ten directions!
I shall now briefly expound this secret method for the elimination of calamities,
which was taught by the World-Honored One as the most excellent and supreme.
To swiftly emerge from birth and death, And quickly realize great enlightenment;
To accord with the realms of sentient beings, And to teach the methods for removing calamities,
increasing reverence, and subjugating others, As well as for women experiencing the difficulties of the postpartum period.
For those in perilous childbirth or afflicted by illness,
where gods and ghosts bring about calamity, one should establish a maṇḍala and fashion or paint an image of the tutelary deity, lighting forty-nine lamps.
Make offerings to the Vaidūrya Honored One, who constantly illuminates day and night;
Present incense, flowers, fruits, and food, and fashion canopies and banners of five colors;
Release sentient beings of water and land for forty-nine full days.
Consecrate five-colored threads and tie them around the patient's neck.
One who wishes to practice this rite should first receive the samaya vows from a master and generate the mind of great bodhicitta.
Having received the vidyādhara initiation and been authorized by the ācārya,
one should then practice in a forest, a secluded place,
by a river, a lake, the seashore, or in one's own dwelling.
Sweep and smear the maṇḍala; arrange it square or circular according to one's intention.
Place two *argha* water vessels and set out the seven lower positions with incense, flowers, lamps, food, drink, and unguents.
Arrange the altar at its four sides; perform repentance, sympathetic joy, entreaty, and the making of vows.
Dedicate all merits so that they may correspondingly achieve *siddhi*, practicing in accordance with the teachings.
The Heart-Secret Mudrā of the Buddha Family: Form the inner-binding gesture with the hands of meditative concentration and wisdom;
extend both index fingers straight upward. Visualize the Buddhas filling all of space, recite the mantra seven times, and then release the mudrā over the crown of the head.
The mantra says:
By virtue of this empowerment, all Buddhas gather like clouds;
their light shines upon the practitioner, who is freed from obstacles and swiftly attains accomplishment.
Next, bind the mudrā of the Lotus Family: form the heart-mudrā as before, but bend the thumb (the *samādhi-wheel*) into the palm; erect the index finger (the *prajñā-wheel*).
One should visualize oneself as Avalokiteśvara together with his lotus retinue.
To the right of all Tathāgatas, one should recite the mantra seven times;
through this empowerment, the assembly of Bodhisattvas will gather like clouds,
acting as companions to the practitioner so that all their aspirations are fulfilled.
Next, bind the mudrā of the Vajra Family. The heart-mudrā is also as before:
bend the wisdom-wheel (the right hand) into the palm and erect the concentration-wheel (the left hand).
One should visualize Vajrapāṇi, the holder of all vajras.
Dwelling to the right of the Tathāgata, recite the mantra seven times;
by virtue of this empowerment, the assembly of Vajra-beings will gather and,
in accordance with the Buddha’s fundamental compassionate vow, protect the practitioner.
The three karmas are like vajras, firm and indestructible.
Next, bind the armor mudrā: form fists for both śamatha and vipaśyanā;
hold the wheels crosswise in the palms, with the śamatha fist placed at the heart.
Visualize the fist and apply it to five places: the forehead, the two shoulders, the heart, and the throat.
By means of this mudrā and mantra, one is empowered and armored;
thus, no māras shall oppress or assail them, and they will swiftly attain accomplishment.
Among all the Buddha-uṣṇīṣas, this seal possesses great majesty;
by merely forming it to protect the body, humans and devas alike will revere and honor you.
In all places of peril and during times of various calamities, [it shall provide protection].
May all beings obtain peace and happiness. Next, with a sincere and devout mind,
extend the wheel of *śamatha*, hold the seal of *vipaśyanā* upon the ground,
and recite the mantra seven times while performing the empowerment.
By transforming this realm of affliction into a pure and wondrous buddha-field through the power of this empowerment, the pure land of the Principal Deity is established,
adorned with various magnificent jewel palaces.
Within the precious palace, visualize the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru surrounded by a host of Bodhisattvas;
contemplate the maṇḍala and then form the mudrā of invitation,
using the heart-mantra of the preceding Buddha-family.
The two wheels turn toward the body; by reciting the mantra three times,
through this empowerment, all those who create obstacles flee far away, and they pay homage to the practitioner.
Next, offer arghya water. Place seasonal flowers floating upon it, along with precious medicinal herbs and fragrant seeds within the water;
holding it up to the crown of the head, offer it while reciting the mantra seven times.
Visualize bathing the feet of the noble assembly and proclaim your desired aspirations;
by offering this fragrant water, you shall leave behind defilement and attain purity,
eventually reaching the stage of consecration and realizing the Dharmakāya of the Tathāgata.
Next, bind the mudrā for offering the seat. Visualize five blossoming flowers emerging from the mudrā;
by means of this mantra and mudrā, the principal deity together with his retinue [occupy] the lotus lion-throne.
Each receives a precious lotus flower and a vajra lion throne;
next, perform the ritual of the Great Seal (Mahāmudrā) for universal offering.
Interlace the tips of the thumbs at first, and from the center of the seal, [the offerings] flow forth.
Various kinds of offerings— incense, flowers, lamps,
ointments, food, drink, and so forth; oceans of clouds of manifold music,
platforms, parasols, jeweled pavilions, and adorned jewel-thrones.
Exquisite victory banners, streamers, and canopies, And jars of virtue filled with various fragrant waters—
All flow forth from the mudrā, Pervading the entirety of space and the dharma-realm,
To make offerings to all the Tathāgatas, Bodhisattvas, and the assembly of noble ones.
Then, with the threefold power, recite these true and wondrous verses with a sincere heart three times;
all shall be accomplished through the power of my merit and the empowerment of the Tathāgata.
And through the power of the *dharmadhātu*, one dwells making universal offerings;
subsequently, one performs the ritual procedure for binding the seal of the Buddha’s Great Compassion (*mahāmaitrī*).
Firmly bind the five crowns (*pañcamuṣṭi*), and join the tips of the supreme wheels (*cakravarti*) upward.
By sealing the heart, forehead, throat, and crown— the very essence of all Buddhas—
through this empowerment, all demonic obstacles, hardships,
and malicious persons who seek to cause harm will swiftly give rise to a mind of loving-kindness.
Next, bind the Buddha-Eye Mudrā: one should hold the two *puṭas* with the two palms facing outward and back-to-back;
like the shape of smiling eyes, bend the two wheels (thumbs) and each hold the joint-texture between the two light-fingers (index fingers).
Seal the five places of one's own body; by this seal and mantra, the Mother Buddha constantly bestows protection.
Through the power of this empowerment, all aspirations are fulfilled and all inauspiciousness is dispelled.
It gives birth to all merit and virtue, And extinguishes all sinful obstructions;
It enables all sentient beings To attain peace and happiness upon seeing or hearing it.
Next, one should proclaim and praise The virtues of the tutelary deity.
I take refuge in the realm of the full moon, the Honored One of pure and wondrous lapis lazuli;
The Dharma-medicine that rescues humans and devas, whose twelve vows in the causal stage were vast in compassionate and grand resolve— May all sentient beings be delivered.
I now offer this praise and extolment; with a sincere heart, I prostrate my head before the fundamental secret mudrā.
Interlace the two palms inwardly, keeping the two wrists slightly apart, opening them by about three or two inches.
Because of this, one should recite the mantra seven times up to one hundred and eight times;
then, while forming the mudrā of scattering at the crown of the head,
one should set forth the heart of one's aspirations before that very deity.
I pray that you will graciously bestow your compassionate gaze, to utterly extinguish calamities and eliminate untimely deaths.
Next, take the rosary and place it within your two palms;
empower it seven times and hold it up to the crown of your head.
By means of this mantra and mudrā, through the empowerment of the rosary,
one begins from the mother bead; for each recitation, one turns one bead,
and when the final syllable of the mantra is completed, one returns to the mother bead.
One should not leap over the mother bead; to leap over it is a transgression of the Dharma.
The extensive teaching consists of eighteen thousand [recitations], which are abbreviated to one hundred and eight.
Once the count is complete, hold the beads again and perform the empowerment.
To fulfill whatever is prayed for, one should sincerely and universally dedicate [the merit].
This is the Dharma-seal mantra.
If good sons and good daughters, etc., [should recite it...]
May all various obstacles and difficulties, all illnesses,
and for women, the perils of difficult childbirth,
be transformed from calamity into fortune.
Furthermore, for those suffering from illnesses caused by malevolent spirits that are difficult to cure,
one should twist together cords of five colors,
recite the mantra over them, and tie them around the patient’s neck, hands, feet, waist, abdomen, and so forth.
Furthermore, one must invite seven monks to establish a ritual site (*maṇḍala*), fashion an image of the Principal Deity,
transcribe the *Bhaiṣajyaguru-sūtra*, and perform the ritual circumambulation at the six times of the day.
Light seven-tiered lamps,
fashion banners of five colors forty-nine feet in length,
and recite the sutra forty-nine times each day.
He released forty-nine aquatic creatures and animals;
at that time, he reverently made offerings of flowers and fruits,
and recited mantras over five-colored threads while making vows.
Furthermore, support the seal upon the cord,
recite the mantra forty-nine more times,
and tie forty-nine knots.
Again, recite this mantra.
The empowerment mantra is as follows:
Furthermore, praise and prostrate to the deity, and bind the secret mudrā of the deity.
Recite the mantra seven times. Again, offer argha water as before and extend the offerings.
Form the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa mudrā and recite the vidyā-mantra three times. Then, release the boundary by turning to the left.
Offer them to the assembly of noble ones. As before, perform the mudrā of invitation by moving the two wheels outward.
Visualize that they return to the pure land within the precious palace of the summer retreat in the midst of space.
Having escorted the principal deity away, one should immediately form the secret mudrā of the Buddha’s Compassionate Protection Samaya.
Then, empower the four places with the empowerment mudrā,
followed by the Buddha-eye mudrā, and finally seal the five places with the mantra mudrā.
Bind the heart-seals (*hṛdaya-mudrā*) of the three families; recite each respective root mantra three times.

Again, bind the armor seal to protect the body. With mantras and seals, seal the five locations, pay homage to the Buddha, and make great vows. Then, as you wish, engage in walking meditation (*caṅkrama*).

The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Medicine Master Tathāgata’s Elimination of Calamities and Removal of Difficulties; one fascicle of the Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Medicine Master Vaiḍūryaprabha Tathāgata’s Elimination of Calamities and Removal of Difficulties.
Composed by the Acharya Ichigyō at the request of Sokuichi, a disciple of Ryōnen of Tōdai-ji.
This is the edition now being carved.
This is the collated edition of the founding master of Lingyun, Venerable Jingyan;
it is hoped that this will be engraved upon printing blocks to be distributed throughout the heavens,
so that the great calamities of the nine types of untimely death may be extinguished all at once.
The chronic ailments of the four great elements were removed in an instant.
Recorded respectfully by the śramaṇa Mudō of the Hōryū-ji temple at Hōjō, in the auspicious day of the twelfth month of the Katsura year (Jia-Yin) during the Enpō era.
